gloss: to be satisfied; to feel at ease; to have one's mind put at rest

definitions.gloss: to be satisfied; to feel at ease; to have one's conscience or feelings settled
definitions.explanation: Describes the state of inner satisfaction or relief that comes when one has done what one feels is necessary or right. Very often used in the negative form {気|き}が{済|す}まない (to not feel right about something; to not be satisfied until something is done).

examples.japanese: {謝|あやま}らないと{気|き}が{済|す}まない。
examples.english: I won't feel right until I apologize.

examples.japanese: {自分|じぶん}で{確認|かくにん}しないと{気|き}が{済|す}まない{性格|せいかく}だ。
examples.english: I have the kind of personality that can't rest until I've checked things myself.

examples.japanese: {言|い}いたいことを{全部|ぜんぶ}{言|い}って、やっと{気|き}が{済|す}んだ。
examples.english: I said everything I wanted to say and finally felt satisfied.

examples.japanese: {彼|かれ}は{完璧|かんぺき}にやらないと{気|き}が{済|す}まないタイプだから、いつも{残業|ざんぎょう}している。
examples.english: He's the type who won't rest until everything is perfect, so he's always working overtime.

notes:
Composed of {気|き} (mind, feeling) + が + {済|す}む (to be finished, to be settled). The negative form {気|き}が{済|す}まない is far more common than the affirmative, used to express a compulsion to do something or dissatisfaction with an incomplete state.

COMMON PATTERNS:
- {気|き}が{済|す}まない: to not feel satisfied; to feel compelled to do something
- 〜しないと{気|き}が{済|す}まない: to not feel right until one does ~
- やっと{気|き}が{済|す}んだ: to finally feel at ease
- {気|き}が{済|す}むまで: until one is satisfied

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {気|き}が{晴|は}れる: to feel refreshed; to feel relieved — focuses on clearing negative emotions
- {納得|なっとく}する: to be convinced; to accept — more intellectual than emotional
- {満足|まんぞく}する: to be satisfied — more general; {気|き}が{済|す}む implies a personal compulsion being resolved
